fieldMarks: Male: black head and back, white bar separating gray sides from black chest
Distinct pale rings on the bill; the brown neck ring is very hard to see
Female mostly gray-brown with a pale area near the bill base and a peaked head
behavior: Springs directly off the water without the running take-off of most diving ducks
Dives in water a few feet deep; also feeds at the surface and in flooded fields
Mixes with other divers on large lakes and with dabblers on shallow water
Migrates in flocks late in fall and early in spring
habitat: Freshwater marshes, ponds and bogs in forest openings in summer; ponds, lakes and slow rivers in winter, generally not salt bays.
range: Breeds from southeastern Alaska and central British Columbia east through northern Saskatchewan to Newfoundland, south to northeastern California, Colorado, Iowa and New England; winters from the southwestern and southeastern U.S. south to Central America. It has become much more widespread as a breeder in eastern Canada and northern New England since the 1930s.
